reason: The text depicts the divine commission of Moses as the leader of the Israelite liberation movement. God explicitly instructs Moses to gather the elders of Israel, negotiate with Pharaoh on behalf of the people, and speak God's words to lead the nation out of Egypt. Though Moses initially objects to the commission, he ultimately accepts the role, takes up the staff of authority, returns to Egypt, and with Aaron, assembles the elders of Israel and delivers God's message. The people then recognize him as their leader, believing and worshipping based on his credentials. The narrative establishes Moses as both the designated and accepted national leader of Israel.
